subject: Inspection schedule, sample sets, and MSA redline coordination
messages:
From: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-team@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-06-30T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: SOC2 scope + pen test window questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile. Our legal and infosec teams are now trying to lock down the assurance language for the MSA and order form. A few concrete asks so we can get the contract queued with procurement: 

- Can you confirm the SOC 2 scope you support (Infrastructure + Application) and whether you will provide the SOC 2 Type II report for the current rolling 12 months?
- We need a proposed sampling plan for the audit: what sample sets do you expect (users, API keys, tenant logs) and typical turnaround for evidence requests?
- Pen test access: legal is asking for a timeboxed window and a minimal-privilege jumpbox approach for staging. Do you have preferred windows and an ops contact?

Attached is our initial checklist so your team can annotate. If you can respond with a short summary and a proposed redline for the MSA audit-rights clause by EOW, that would help move the review along.

Attachment: [initial_security_questions.pdf (PDF)]

Best,
Kate Lawson
Head of Vendor Security
Acme Health Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 scope + pen test window questions

Hi Kate — thanks for the checklist, sharing internally and looping in Karthik (legal) + Soojin (ops). High level answers and next steps below: 

1) SOC 2 scope: Infrastructure (hosted runtime), Application (API surface), Controls around logging and access management are in scope; we will provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the last 12 months.

2) Sampling / inspection plan:
- Proposed sample sets:
  * Tenant configuration changes (sample of 5 tenants over last 6 months)
  * API call logs (3 x 24-hour slices representative of peak/normal/low)
  * RBAC changes (all admin role changes in the last 90 days)
- Evidence cadence: standard turnaround is 48 hours for document-level requests; for scoped log exports we typically need up to 5 business days depending on retention window and redaction needs.

3) Pen test window & jumpbox:
- We can offer a 2-week staging window; preferred start dates: 2026-07-12 or 2026-07-26.
- Access: limited-privilege jumpbox + ephemeral creds; ops contact will be Soojin (see below).

4) MSA redline: attached a short summary of the proposed audit-rights language that limits scope to systems that process Acme data, requires prior notice for inspection (48-72 hours), and sets a 2-week window for remediation before broader production-level inspection. This is intended to keep the contract operationally feasible for Redwood while meeting your needs.

Action items: 
- Kate: confirm which pen-test start date you'd prefer and whether the 48-hour document SLA is acceptable.
- Legal: confirm if we should add an escrow for third-party evidence pulls (we can include in order form as an opt-in).
- Marissa/Legal: we'll open a shared drive and put the proposed redline (proposed_audit_scope_v1.docx) there for inline comments.

Attachments: [proposed_audit_scope_v1.docx (DOCX)]

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Office: +1 415-555-0102

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@acmecorp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 scope + pen test window questions

Thanks — quick legal follow-up and suggested redline bullets. Quoting Marissa's plan above for context.

Suggested redline bullets for MSA audit-rights exhibit (high level):
- Audit rights limited to systems and logs that contain or process Acme data; no unrestricted access to Redwood internal customer data.
- Requests for evidence to be made via a shared ticket in our security queue with 48-72 hour response SLA for document requests and up to 5 business days for curated log extracts.
- Pen test: require a scoping call 7 days prior; require test plan and IP ranges; testing limited to staging environment and subject to an ops-approved jumpbox.
- Confidentiality and nondisclosure: pen-test reports are shared under mutual NDA and may be redacted by Redwood for internal tenant identifiers.
- Escalation: if high-severity findings are discovered, Redwood will notify within 24 hours and propose a remediation roadmap within 3 business days.

I attached a short .txt summarizing the redline points to speed inline review. If Acme legal wants these converted into tracked changes in the MSA I can get the legal team to produce a marked-up doc.

Attachment: [msa_redline_summary.txt (text)]

- Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: legalops@acmecorp.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@acmecorp.com>, security-team@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-07-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 scope + pen test window questions

Marissa/Karthik — appreciate the clear summary. Acme legal has reviewed the bullets and can accept the limited-scope audit rights and the evidence cadence you proposed with two small edits: 

1) We need the 48-hour SLA for document requests to be documented as a "best-effort" SLA tied to reasonable redaction and legal review.
2) For pen-testing, Acme requires a single 72-hour escalation contact window post-test for critical issues before public disclosure (to align with our enterprise policy).

If you can accept those two adjustments we'll sign the MSA redline. We've routed a DocuSign envelope for the MSA update here: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-msa-redline. A signed PDF will follow; we've included a signed confirmation for the scope in the envelope.

Attachment: [signed_msa_redline.pdf (PDF)]

Please confirm acceptance of the two edits and we will proceed to execution.

Regards,
Acme Legal Operations
legalops@acmecorp.com
